docs.title: Choose the query for the question
docs.text:
All seven queries read already committed facts. None reruns the proposer or evaluator.

Query Question it answers Requires a rankable result? best() Which artifact won on the primary objective? Yes best_trial() What metrics and evidence belong to that winner? Yes lineage() Which causal path produced an artifact? Only when no target is supplied trials() What happened on every seed evaluation and proposal attempt? No summary() What portable score, usage, and identity summary describes the run? Yes inspect() What was declared, attempted, spent, and failed? No compare() How do two compatible run summaries differ? Yes, on both sides

The output shows the winner at logical step 1, whose lineage is the seed at step 0 followed by that successor. Three evaluated states mean the seed and two proposal trials all produced measurements. complete/rankable says the run stopped normally and has at least one usable metric.

An objective name passed to best("timeline") or best_trial("timeline") queries that declared metric instead of the primary overall metric. It does not change how the run originally ranked candidates.

docs.title: Diagnose a run without a winner
docs.text: best(), best_trial(), lineage() without a target, and summary() raise NoSuccessfulEvaluation when no evaluation has metrics. trials() and inspect() still work and preserve each typed failure. That is why the example catches NoSuccessfulEvaluation and then prints two EvaluatorFailure records: the evaluator failed for both the seed and the attempted successor.

docs.title: Change one query and predict
docs.text:
Print result.best_trial("timeline").metrics["timeline"] in main(). The value is 1.0: the query selects on the declared timeline metric, while the stored trials and the original primary-objective winner remain unchanged.

Next, grade with checks and rubrics.

docs.title: Custom search
docs.text:
Use @meta.search when a policy needs only seed/incumbent selection, expansion, and an explicit stop. The component playground is the canonical executable example.

Implement the full SearchProgram.next(state) protocol only when a current job needs decisions the facade cannot express. A custom program returns typed trial, archive, or stop decisions; it does not invoke proposers, evaluate candidates, mutate projections, or allocate beyond state.remaining_budget.

Keep configuration canonical and identity-visible, use recorded named random substreams, and pass the policy conformance suite. The coordinator must remain unchanged when the custom policy is installed.

docs.title: Project status
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. Meta-Evolve currently ships the dependency-free local author surface through Milestone 10.9: callable and expanded experiments, replaceable search and context, typed failures, exact budgets, experience, durable local execution, external command evaluation, whole-workspace editing, inspection, comparisons, CLI, and the optional read-only browser.

Harness evolution has deterministic shipped machinery plus explicitly labeled live-only demonstrations. Later tree search, trusted distributed workers, and federation remain design work. The milestones own sequence and acceptance gates; the programming model owns the shipped public contract. Design records cannot override either.

The current documentation overhaul changes examples and teaching ownership, not the production API. No rubric API, provider package, Git artifact, or new root export is introduced.

docs.title: Local run browser
docs.text: M10.7–M10.8 provide an optional, read-only presentation over shipped Storage, inspection, artifact presentation, diff, comparison, and exact-version contracts.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text:
Install the optional dependencies, then point the command at an existing durable store:

uv sync --extra browser
meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --port 8000

Runs using a custom artifact codec can reconstruct it through the ordinary experiment-module convention:

meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --module experiments.my_run

The optional module is loaded only after browser dependencies are available. Only its experiment().registry enters the browser reader; proposers, evaluators, policies, sessions, and execution are never invoked. Without the module or codec, the run is an ordinary actionable codec-unavailable 422 state rather than corruption.

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The host is fixed to loopback and the server uses one worker. The browser has no write, run, resume, cancellation, promotion, or deletion controls. It has no authentication. Loopback binding limits its intended scope; it is not a claim that the application is safe to proxy or publish remotely.

The pages are complete server-rendered HTML. Search, detail, comparison, lineage tables, and navigation work with JavaScript disabled. A small same-origin script only polls committed stream versions and reloads after facts change. A complete run page with a stable version carries no polling attributes at all; only the catalog and incomplete or unstable pages poll.

docs.title: What appears
docs.text:
The catalog is ordered lexicographically by content-derived run ID; it makes no chronological claim. Cards show task identity, lifecycle, rankability, policy, the primary objective and available score, artifact kind, and usage. Search filters those recorded fields.

A detail page follows the recorded story: overview, declaration, lineage, trials, evidence and failures, recorded artifact history, and decision timeline. The SVG lineage diagram has a semantic table containing the same parent edges. The history table preserves recorded occurrence order without calling it time, keeps occurrence identity separate from content digest, and offers one explicit diff choice for every parent.

Artifact pages show identity, parents, bounded specialized presentation, exact canonical attachment, and every available parent diff. Text, source trees, skill sets, canonical Python values, harnesses, and policy artifacts have fixed views. A custom kind receives deterministic canonical-payload text and an explicit no-specialized-view notice. All content originates in the frozen payload; decoded ArtifactView.value is never read, stringified, or passed to templates. Evidence URIs remain inert text, never links.

Direct-parent diffs support Text, SourceTree, and SkillSet. They identify added, removed, modified, and unchanged files and label added, removed, and unchanged lines textually as well as visually. A file whose content is identical on both sides reports its unchanged status without lines and consumes none of the shared diff budgets. Foreign-run views, non-parent edges, and incompatible families are refused with 422. Multi-parent occurrences never acquire an arbitrary default parent.

Bounds apply in this order: lexicographic path sorting; first 100 entries; 64 KiB UTF-8 per retained preview document; 256 KiB aggregate preview input; 64 KiB per diff side and 256 KiB aggregate diff input before invoking the diff algorithm; then 4,000 output lines. Final partial and omitted states remain visible. Canonical downloads are not truncated.

Comparison always receives an explicit ordered pair and invokes the public Run.compare() contract. It reports score, usage, winner or tie, and the three declaration flags. Incompatible or unrankable pairs remain visible as typed refusals; the browser does not pre-filter candidates or turn failure into a score.

docs.title: Replay and caches
docs.text:
One dedicated thread creates Storage.read_only(), performs every listing, version query, inspection, and comparison, and closes the handle. Route handlers and Starlette's general threadpool never receive it. This preserves SQLite connection affinity while concurrent HTTP requests queue safely.

The first catalog request performs one validated replay for every discovered run. It keeps one lightweight card per run, stamped with the exact run_version it observed and replaced when a newer version appears, plus a 32-entry LRU of full inspections. Comparisons use a separate 32-entry LRU keyed by the ordered IDs and both exact versions. Eviction discards only derived views, never durable facts. Inspections retain each frozen payload beside the decoded object, without eagerly storing an additional serialized byte copy; payload-heavy runs therefore consume proportionally more memory inside the bounded LRU. A comparison cache miss pays the public API's full multi-replay cost.

Before replay, the reader polls exact versions. Exact hits avoid replay; completed cached runs are not polled again. Catalog polling still calls Storage.runs() to discover additions and checks versions of incomplete runs.

Inspection reads a version before and after replay. A mismatch is retried once. If commits continue, the valid inspection snapshot is served without a version label or cache entry. Comparison is stricter: both versions must remain stable across the complete public comparison. A second mismatch returns retryable 503 rather than presenting a mixed observation.

docs.title: Failures and safety
docs.text:
Unknown or concurrently missing runs and artifact occurrences return 404. Comparison and diff refusals and codec capability gaps return escaped 422 pages. Transient store failures and unstable comparisons return 503. Corruption and unexpected defects return a safe 500 without a traceback or durable detail. A corrupt or codec-unavailable run becomes an isolated catalog error card so healthy runs remain reachable.

Store-open and schema failures happen before the server binds and use the ordinary CLI domain-failure path. Responses include a restrictive content security policy, nosniff, no-referrer, and frame-denial headers. These defenses do not expand the browser beyond its local, unauthenticated scope.

Raw artifact responses use application/json, nosniff, and Content-Disposition: attachment with a digest-derived filename. The bytes are the current digest encoding, canonical-payload-v1, not a native artifact export and not an unconditional promise for every future durable format.

docs.title: Manual visual review checklist
docs.text:
For changes to browser templates or CSS, review the catalog, run, artifact, diff, refusal, truncation, and codec-unavailable fixtures with JavaScript disabled at both fixed viewports:

  • desktop: 1440 × 900;
  • mobile: 390 × 844.

Record completion in the PR. Check heading order, landmarks, skip link, visible keyboard focus, native controls, textual status labels, contained wide tables and preformatted text, single-column mobile layout, and reduced-motion mode. Screenshot automation remains out of scope for this milestone.

docs.title: Durability
docs.text:
Storage composes artifact and event storage. In-memory storage is isolated to the process. Durable storage uses a verified filesystem artifact store plus an append-only SQLite event stream.

import meta_evolve as meta

storage = meta.Storage.durable(".meta-evolve/example")

docs.title: Store
docs.text: Pass durable storage to meta.run() to preserve committed artifacts, evidence, decisions, lineage, usage, and failures. mode="durable-local" additionally requires registered reconstructible components and their verified manifests. Validation happens before the first event is written.

docs.title: Reopen
docs.text:
Run reconstructs a read-only view from committed facts:

reopened = meta.Run(run_id, storage)
print(reopened.summary())

Reopen performs no proposal or evaluation. Local callable and SDK histories can be durable and inspectable even when their live components cannot be rebuilt.

For an inspection-only process, open the same directory without commit or execution authority:

with meta.Storage.read_only(".meta-evolve/example") as storage:
    version = storage.run_version(run_id)
    inspection = meta.Run(run_id, storage).inspect()

is_durable and is_read_only answer different questions. The first says committed facts live on durable media; the second says this handle cannot commit. Storage.durable(...) reports True, False, while Storage.read_only(...) reports True, True. Artifact, blob, event, and unit-of-work writes all raise CapabilityError. Passing the handle to run(), improve(), or resume() is rejected before a codec, registry component, proposer, evaluator, provider, or subprocess runs.

run_version(run_id) is the maximum committed event sequence. It returns 0 for a well-formed id with no events and uses a new deferred transaction on each call, so a long-lived reader observes successive atomic commits from a WAL writer. It is deliberately a cheap polling query, not a full integrity check. Run(run_id, storage).inspect() performs authoritative loading and still raises RunNotFound when that run is required but absent.

The optional local run browser owns one long-lived read-only handle on one dedicated thread. It calls runs() to discover additions, polls exact versions before replay, and never polls a cached completed run again. Its bounded caches are disposable observations; append-only storage and validated replay remain authoritative.

Read-only open requires an existing current store. It uses SQLite mode=ro plus query_only, and never creates a directory, changes journal settings, executes DDL, stamps a schema, or migrates. For an older or unstamped store, close readers and reopen it once with writable Storage.durable(...), then use Storage.read_only(...) again. Future schemas raise SchemaVersionRejected, malformed current schemas raise DurableCorruption, and missing or inaccessible database/filesystem/WAL state raises DurableStoreError with the underlying cause.

docs.title: Resume
docs.text:
resume verifies manifests, declarations, store integrity, and the recovery frontier before doing missing work. It retains the same run ID and never re-executes a committed operation. A non-resumable local history raises CapabilityError.

Use internal Session.resume to pace that same recovery:

from meta_evolve.application.runtime import Session

with Session.resume(run_id, storage=storage, registry=registry) as session:
    for decision in session:
        observe(decision)
result = session.run

Preparation validates and classifies the committed frontier but does not finish pending work. The first step() either completes the already committed trial or evaluation, or records and completes one new decision. Resuming an already stopped run iterates zero times; an explicit terminal step() returns the existing stop view without changing events or artifacts.

docs.title: Compare
docs.text: Reopened completed runs use the same comparison contract as live results. Declaration mismatches raise RunsNotComparable before ranking.

docs.title: Replay and reproducibility
docs.text:
Replay is a pure fold over immutable transitions and artifacts. It reconstructs logical decisions, projections, context selection, access audits, and usage without calling external systems. Named random streams reproduce deterministic local choices. Provider output is not promised to regenerate byte-for-byte; the durable guarantee is the exact committed transcript and declarations.

Corrupt bytes, unknown schemas, gaps, mismatched IDs, and incomplete atomic batches fail explicitly rather than falling back to a partial interpretation.

docs.title: Experience
docs.text: Experience is explicit and off by default. The growing tutorial pushes ancestor failures in Use failures; this page is the lookup for every shipped memory policy.

docs.title: No memory
docs.text: With no context= or experience= declaration, a proposer receives no prior records. NoMemory states that policy explicitly when a named declaration is useful.

docs.title: Pushed context
docs.text:
A ContextPolicy selects a bounded bundle before each proposal. AncestorsOnly follows the current parent lineage; BestSibling exposes a bounded sibling view. The selected structured records, rendered text, reason, logical time, and usage are committed before the proposer runs.

import meta_evolve as meta

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed=seed,
    proposer=proposer,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
    context=meta.policies.AncestorsOnly(max_records=4, max_chars=4000),
)
result = meta.run(experiment)

docs.title: Audited pull
docs.text: PullAccess grants bounded operations, result counts, records, and characters. The proposer uses an ExperienceReader only inside that grant. Each request, result, denial, and usage charge is retained; hidden or future records fail closed through typed access errors.

docs.title: Declared derivation
docs.text: A rich proposal may declare which authorized observations influenced it. Those references are validated against the experience it actually received. Empty derivation remains compatible with ordinary callables.

docs.title: Causal provenance
docs.text:
Everyday users can rely on Run.lineage(), Run.trials(), and meta_evolve.views.RunExperienceUsage. Strict ledger ordering, logical-time validation, and replay are isolated in the advanced provenance reference.

Experience changes what a proposer may observe, never the evaluator, budget, permission, or promotion authority.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text: Add replaceable components at declared seams; never branch the coordinator on a concrete domain, provider, evaluator, policy, or backend.

docs.title: Artifact domains
docs.text:
An artifact codec declares a stable kind, representation, interfaces, canonical encode/decode behavior, and rejection boundary. Register it with Registry. The same codec encodes the seed and every successor; rejected values become typed invalid-output trials.

The complete artifact-domain tutorial is extracted, executed in a clean interpreter, and checked against the published codec conformance suite.

docs.title: Components and identity
docs.text: Local callables are convenient but not cold-resumable. Registered durable-local proposers, evaluators, search policies, and context policies use explicit component references plus behavior-affecting configuration. Resume rebuilds the recorded implementation from that registry and refuses mismatches.

docs.title: Published conformance
docs.text:
Every extension component family has a published reusable suite: codecs, repository-editing proposers, evaluators, search programs, context policies, workspaces, sandboxes, and typed mutation surfaces. Subclass one, name the subclass Test..., and override its fixtures and hooks. Each runs unchanged here against the built-in implementations (or, for the proposer suites, reference callables) plus at least one written the way an outside author would write it. Generic mutation conformance remains exercised against policy controls such as ParentSelection and TrialLimit; SearchProgramTests against Greedy, BestOfN, Population, CandidatePolicy, and a next-only custom program.

The two proposer suites are exercised by in-repository reference callables (tests/test_proposer_conformance.py); no first-party provider adapter ships, so those callables are the reference subjects.

SandboxProviderTests checks the declared cwd and exact environment, verbatim argv, separated output streams, ordinary nonzero exits, enforced timeout, independent stdout/stderr byte ceilings, bounded partial output, and wall-only usage. Its timeout and probe-sleep fixtures are overridable for container and remote startup costs. Passing it does not prove filesystem isolation or that a provider executed rather than simulated every probe; CPU, memory, network, syscall, and broader execution isolation remain outside the suite.

ContextPolicy.select receives a typed, read-only ExperienceGraph. Advanced extensions import ExperienceGraph and ExperienceQuery from meta_evolve.application.experience; neither is part of the 24-name root surface. Replay construction also remains an application service.

State the limits rather than implying coverage that does not exist. A suite checks the laws it names and no others, and it makes an unexercised law visible: EvaluatorTests skips its typed-failure check when a subclass declares no rejected_candidates and its semantic oracle when it declares no scored_candidates, ArtifactCodecTests skips its aliasing law when mutable_values is () and its decode-validation law when rejected_payloads is (), and ContextPolicyTests makes a policy that selects nothing say so through expects_records. NoMemory is outside that suite, since meta.run normalizes it away before any policy runs.

The subclass contract follows one rule set, stated in the package docstring: required hooks raise NotImplementedError; optional laws skip visibly or cross-check a declaration; a law needing an uncontaminated second subject asks for a factory (make_evaluator, search_factory) and refuses the same object twice; laws observe subjects through kernel records or author-supplied projections, never the subject's own equality or self-report.

One trap is worth knowing when you write a codec: decode returning an equal value is not the same as returning an independent one. A codec that hands back the instance it was given lets an evaluator reach and edit the caller's own object. ArtifactCodecTests.mutable_values has no default for that reason — declaring () is a positive claim that your values are immutable, not a way to skip the question. Every value law observes through value_state, an observation the codec has no hand in — never through the value type's __eq__ (which usually ships with the codec and could certify a collapse) and never through the codec's own encode (which could special-case the watched objects); the default projection knows exact canonical and kernel types and refuses anything else. Mutable values additionally require mutate, the edit the aliasing law watches. rejected_payloads is the mirror of rejected_values on the decode side — decode is validation, and () is a positive claim that every payload decodes. EvaluatorTests.scored_candidates is the analogous semantic oracle: every other evaluator law holds for lambda c: 0.0, so state expected metrics wherever your scores are predictable. EvaluatorTests keeps a matching candidate-mutation law, so the failure is caught where it starts and where it does damage.

Store adapters keep an internal contract under tests/ and are not one of these families. The operations reference holds the coverage table.

docs.title: Migrating pre-1.0 conformance subclasses
docs.text:
The strengthened codec and mutation-surface laws intentionally changed their subclass fixtures. There are no compatibility aliases: update subclasses so the new laws run instead of silently retaining the weaker contract.

For codecs, rejected_payloads and mutable_values are now required. value_state must project custom values the default inert projection cannot read, and mutate is required only when mutable_values is non-empty.

Before:

class TestRecipeCodec(ArtifactCodecTests):
    @pytest.fixture
    def codec(self): return RecipeCodec()

    @pytest.fixture
    def values(self): return (Recipe(["mix"]),)

    @pytest.fixture
    def rejected_values(self): return (7,)

After:

class TestRecipeCodec(ArtifactCodecTests):
    # codec, values, and rejected_values stay as above
    @pytest.fixture
    def rejected_payloads(self): return (7, None)

    @pytest.fixture
    def mutable_values(self): return (Recipe(["mix"]),)

    def value_state(self, value): return tuple(value.steps)

    def mutate(self, value): value.steps.append("bake")

Return () from mutable_values for an immutable value type and omit mutate. Return () from rejected_payloads only when every canonical payload is valid input to decode; both empty tuples are positive claims.

For mutation surfaces, replace the singular mutation plus expected_surface fixtures with plural (mutation, expected_successor) pairs, and replace invalid_mutation with invalid_mutations.

Before:

@pytest.fixture
def mutation(self): return Rename("new")

@pytest.fixture
def expected_surface(self): return NameParam("new")

@pytest.fixture
def invalid_mutation(self): return Rename(7)

After:

@pytest.fixture
def mutations(self):
    return ((Rename("first"), NameParam("first")),
            (Rename("second"), NameParam("second")))

@pytest.fixture
def invalid_mutations(self):
    return (Rename(7),)

Keep surface, no_op_mutation, and foreign_mutation unchanged. Supply more than one valid pair wherever the domain allows, so an implementation that accepts one fixture value but substitutes its own value for others cannot pass.

docs.title: Design rule
docs.text:
Introduce a protocol only when a current acceptance test needs an independently testable second implementation. Keep the public call smaller than the internal port, preserve immutable inputs and typed failures, and make authority and accounting explicit.

The generated API reference lists every shipped root name and the namespaced harness and policy families. See the harness evolution and policy evolution guides.

docs.title: Harness evolution
docs.text:
Harness v2 is the built-in plain-data harness domain.

The author story is ordinary immutable Python:

from dataclasses import replace
import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.harness import Harness

seed = Harness("Make a conservative change.", {"diagnostics": False})

def revise(parent, _context):
    return replace(parent, planner="Inspect tests, then repair.")

result = meta.improve(
    seed=seed, proposer=revise, evaluator=lambda value: len(value.planner), trials=1
)
print(result.best().value)

The model freezes context_policy. Its harness-v2 codec independently accepts only payloads containing planner and context_policy, requires exactly one parent, and rejects malformed or no-op successors as InvalidOutput. Both fields may change together. Harness content contains no component, evaluator, budget, or governance authority; those declarations stay with Task and Experiment.

docs.title: Held-out comparison
docs.text: Search uses development evaluation. Evaluate the unchanged baseline and the selected value in separate seed-only Greedy(max_trials=0) runs, then call meta_evolve.harness.compare_harnesses. Strict comparison requires equal evaluator, artifact, objective, budgets, proposer, search, randomness, context, and experience declarations. The verdict is improvement, tie, regression, or unrankable; eligibility never deploys anything.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
meta_evolve.harness.export_harness writes exactly three files: planner text, context-policy JSON, and a v2 manifest. load_harness strictly validates those files and the content digest. There is no v1 compatibility codec: opening an old harness-manifest-v1 run reports the ordinary codec-unavailable CapabilityError.

Repository episode records belong to the deterministic example rather than the library. Run its complete development and held-out story with:

uv run python examples/research/harness_evolution/main.py --output /tmp/meta-evolve-m8

docs.title: Policy evolution
docs.text: Milestone 9 evaluates tiny declarative search-policy artifacts. Candidates never supply executable policy source.

docs.title: Declare the trusted artifact
docs.text:
from meta_evolve import policy

candidate = policy.PolicyArtifact(
    parent_selection=policy.ParentSelection("incumbent"),
    trial_limit=policy.TrialLimit(2),
)

The schema fixes both surface names, component declarations, interfaces, and allowed domains. PolicyMutation changes exactly one value. Wrapper-side apply() is convenient, while the built-in codec independently validates the encoded successor before artifact commit.

docs.title: Interpret it through an ordinary run
docs.text:
import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve import policy

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=episode.task,
    seed=episode.seed,
    proposer=episode.proposer,
    search=policy.CandidatePolicy(candidate),
    random_seed=episode.random_seed,
)
result = meta.run(experiment, budget=episode.budget)

seed parent selection behaves like independent best-of-N. incumbent behaves like greedy expansion. The artifact's trial limit is voluntary: the evaluator- owned inner budget remains authoritative. The canonical artifact payload is the registered candidate-policy@1 configuration, so durable reconstruction uses the existing policy registry and resume path.

docs.title: Capture episodes without adding a runtime
docs.text:
PolicyEpisode declares a task, canonically encoded seed, proposer, budget, random seed, and evaluator-owned environment. PolicySuite requires non-empty, unique development and held-out splits. Registered references are portable; local closures remain valid only for local composition.

User code executes ordinary meta.run() calls and records EpisodeOutcome values. Each outcome retains its inner RunId, evaluator-owned storage location, policy digest, quality, uncertainty, exact inner usage, typed failure or incomplete state, and exact-completed-run reuse flag. Development may reopen an exact completed run. Held-out execution uses a new empty namespace and never consults development results.

PolicyEvaluation recomputes aggregation from every outcome. A failed, incomplete, or missing episode makes the aggregate non-rankable without discarding partial evidence. Inner trials and evaluations stay inner usage; only actual tokens and elapsed time appear in outer_usage.

docs.title: Compare untouched held-out evidence
docs.text:
Evaluate the unchanged baseline and selected candidate in separate seed-only outer runs using Greedy(max_trials=0), then compare them:

comparison = meta.policy.compare_policies(baseline_run, candidate_run)

Comparison fails closed on changed suites, splits, evaluator/aggregation identity, schemas, objectives, proposers, candidate-policy@1, effective budgets, environments, randomness, context, experience, or immutable surface declarations. Verdicts are improvement, tie, regression, or unrankable. compare_policies returns this report. promotion_eligible requires a strict, fully rankable improvement under equal controls. It reports evidence and never promotes or deploys.

Run the deterministic multi-episode flagship:

uv run python examples/research/policy_evolution/main.py --output /tmp/meta-evolve-m9

docs.title: Bound cost
docs.text:
Use trials= on improve() for the beginner limit. On an expanded experiment, declare all meters the task permits and optionally narrow them per run:

task = meta.Task(
    evaluator=grade,
    objectives=(meta.Maximize("quality", satisfy=1.0),),
    budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=9, trials=8, tokens=20_000, wall_seconds=120),
)

result = meta.run(experiment, budget=meta.Budget(trials=3, wall_seconds=30))

satisfy= stops when the primary objective reaches its threshold. A run budget may narrow but never widen the task budget. Usage is committed and available in summary(), inspect(), and each trial. Count the expensive resource directly: tokens if provider tokens dominate, wall time for bounded agent sessions, and evaluations when graders are costly.

A resource limit is not a low score. It remains a typed unrankable outcome.

docs.title: Choose search
docs.text:
Search decides which parent to expand and when to stop; it never evaluates or mutates artifacts itself.

greedy = meta.Greedy(max_trials=8)
best_of_n = meta.policies.BestOfN(max_trials=8)
population = meta.policies.Population(size=3, tournament_size=2, max_trials=8)

Use Greedy for iterative refinement, BestOfN for independent attempts from the seed, and Population when temporarily worse branches must remain available. Compare policies only under the same effective task and budget.

For a small custom parent rule, use the functional facade:

@meta.search(max_trials=4, parent="incumbent")
def refine(search):
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)

The configuration is durable and identity-visible. Full custom programs belong in Going further.

docs.title: Use the CLI and browser
docs.text:
An experiment module exposes a side-effect-free experiment() factory. The CLI owns storage and execution:

uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/persistence_recovery/experiment.py --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve inspect <run-id> --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve resume <run-id> --module examples/operations/persistence_recovery/resumable.py --storage ./store

Use list to recover run ids and compare for compatible runs. resume requires a durable-local declaration with registered components; inspect is read-only and works for incomplete or unrankable histories.

Install the optional browser dependencies, then start its read-only UI:

uv sync --extra browser
uv run meta-evolve ui --storage ./store

It binds to loopback, renders inert stored data, and has no execution, resume, promotion, deletion, or remote-control authority. See the browser operations reference for deployment limits.

docs.title: Give proposals feedback
docs.text:
Pushed feedback is explicit and bounded. AncestorsOnly renders eligible records from causal ancestors into context.bundle:

from meta_evolve.policies import AncestorsOnly

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed=seed,
    proposer=proposer,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=4),
    context=AncestorsOnly(max_records=10, max_chars=4_000),
)

The proposer can read context.bundle.records or the bounded serialized context.bundle.rendered. It cannot see future results, hidden tests, or records outside the declared policy. A feedback set reused during search is development evidence, not held-out evidence.

Pull access and explicit derivation are advanced authorizations covered in Experience and derivation.

docs.title: Persist and resume
docs.text:
Save a local run by passing durable storage:

with meta.Storage.durable("./run-store") as storage:
    result = meta.run(experiment, storage=storage)
    print(result.id)

This records the history but does not make arbitrary live callables resumable. For mode="durable-local", register deterministic, retry-safe, module-level components in a Registry; a later process can then verify them and call meta.resume(run_id, storage=storage, registry=registry).

Resume continues one existing run under its original authority and budgets. It does not start a new experiment, widen limits, or reinterpret partial failures. Crash-frontier and session mechanics are covered in Durability internals.

docs.title: Use your own SDK
docs.text:
Meta-Evolve owns no provider dependency. Wrap your SDK at the proposer seam and return a normal candidate or use its working-directory mode:

def build_agent(instructions):
    def edit(cwd, context):
        sdk.run(
            instructions=instructions,
            cwd=cwd,
            timeout_seconds=30,
        )
    return WorkspaceProposer(edit)

Keep model id, timeout, tool permissions, and other behavior-affecting settings inside an explicit configured component identity. Otherwise two closures with the same Python name may compare as if they were the same component. Map SDK timeouts, policy refusals, resource limits, and infrastructure faults to the matching typed outcome; do not silently retry or score them as zero.

The deterministic fixture and this live wrapper occupy the same build_agent(...) seam in the code-repair job.

docs.title: Write an evaluator
docs.text:
An evaluator receives a decoded candidate and independently returns one of three supported score shapes:

def scalar(candidate):
    return 0.75

def mapping(candidate):
    return {"quality": 0.75, "length": len(candidate)}

def rich(candidate):
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"quality": 0.75},
        evidence=(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="checks/v1", data={"passed": 3}),),
        usage=meta.Usage(tokens=120),
    )

A scalar maps to the task's primary metric. A mapping records every declared metric. EvaluationResult additionally carries uncertainty, evidence, usage, or a typed failure. Return poor scores for valid but poor work. Return a typed failure for output that cannot be judged, or let an unexpected exception be recorded as evaluator failure.

The task's first objective alone controls default ranking and stopping. Use run.best("metric") or run.best_trial("metric") to query another declared objective. For hard checks and held-out grading, see Grade with checks and rubrics.

docs.title: Write a proposer
docs.text:
The smallest proposer accepts a parent and returns one successor:

def revise(parent):
    return parent + " One concrete next action."

Accept context when the proposal needs recorded randomness, the logical step, declared objectives, pushed records, or authorized experience:

def revise(parent, context):
    choice = context.rng.choice(("today", "within one business day"))
    return f"{parent} I will act {choice}."

Do not let the proposer grade, expand its budget, promote itself, or read hidden evaluator state. Raise an exception only for a proposer fault; return a candidate for valid work even when you expect it to score poorly.

For repository-shaped work, wrap a cwd callback in WorkspaceProposer; see Repair code with an agent.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
You will let a coding agent edit a private working directory while an external grader—not the candidate or agent—decides whether the captured project passes.

The project contains a buggy interval-merging function and an obsolete file. The evaluator-owned tests live outside the candidate snapshot. The shipped “agent” is deterministic so the example runs offline, but it uses the same working-directory callback a live SDK wrapper would use.

docs.title: Start at the agent seam
docs.text:
The callback is the integration seam:

def edit(cwd: Path, context) -> None:
    ...  # edit, add, and remove any number of files

proposer = WorkspaceProposer(edit)

One iteration has a strict boundary: parent snapshot → private workspace → many edits → one captured successor. SourceTree is the immutable UTF-8 snapshot saved after that iteration, not an API for individual agent edits.

Owner Can control Cannot control Agent callback Files inside its private working directory Grader, tests, budget, selection, deployment WorkspaceProposer Materialize the parent and capture one successor Decide whether the successor passes CommandEvaluator Run the external grader and record its result Edit the candidate workspace Experiment Task, budget, search, feedback policy Candidate file contents

docs.title: Complete offline program
docs.text:
"""Repair a Python project through one private-workspace agent iteration."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.adapters import WorkspaceProposer
from meta_evolve.policies import AncestorsOnly
from meta_evolve.ports import Proposer


HERE = Path(__file__).parent
CANDIDATE = HERE / "candidate"
GRADER = HERE / "grader.py"
RUNNER = HERE / "run_grader.py"
MAX_TRIALS = 2
AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30.0
INSTRUCTIONS = (
    "Repair the interval project. The public failure evidence says touching "
    "inclusive intervals are not merged. You may edit, add, or remove files."
)


def edit(cwd: Path, context: meta.ProposerContext) -> None:
    """Deterministic stand-in for an SDK agent that owns a working directory."""

    source = (cwd / "intervals.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    (cwd / "intervals.py").write_text(
        source.replace("start < merged[-1][1]", "start <= merged[-1][1]"),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    (cwd / "obsolete.py").unlink()
    (cwd / "REPAIR.md").write_text(
        f"Used {len(context.bundle.records)} pushed records.\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    cache = cwd / "__pycache__"
    cache.mkdir()
    (cache / "intervals.pyc").write_bytes(b"temporary bytecode")
    (cwd / "loose.pyc").write_bytes(b"temporary bytecode")


def fixture_agent(_instructions: str) -> Proposer:
    return WorkspaceProposer(edit)


def grading_task(grader: Path = GRADER) -> meta.Task:
    evaluator = meta.CommandEvaluator(
        (sys.executable, str(RUNNER), str(grader)),
        environment="python-interval-tests@1",
    )
    return meta.Task(
        evaluator=evaluator,
        artifact=meta.SourceTree,
        objectives=(meta.Maximize("score", satisfy=1),),
        budget=meta.Budget(
            evaluations=MAX_TRIALS + 1,
            trials=MAX_TRIALS,
            wall_seconds=AGENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS * (MAX_TRIALS + 1),
        ),
    )


def repair_project(
    build_agent: Callable[[str], Proposer],
    *,
    grader: Path = GRADER,
) -> meta.Run:
    return meta.run(
        meta.Experiment(
            task=grading_task(grader),
            seed=meta.load_source_tree(CANDIDATE),
            proposer=build_agent(INSTRUCTIONS),
            search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=MAX_TRIALS),
            context=AncestorsOnly(max_records=10, max_chars=4_000),
        )
    )


def main() -> None:
    result = repair_project(fixture_agent)
    winner = result.best().value
    print(f"passed={result.best_trial().metrics['score'] == 1.0}")
    print(f"files={tuple(winner)}")
    print(f"bytecode={any(path.endswith('.pyc') for path in winner)}")
    print(f"feedback={winner['REPAIR.md'].strip()}")
    print(f"evaluations={result.summary().evaluation_count}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

passed=True means the selected successor received score=1.0. The captured file list proves that one iteration changed the whole project: intervals.py was edited, REPAIR.md was added, and obsolete.py was deleted. bytecode=False shows that temporary .pyc and __pycache__ debris was removed before capture. Two evaluations were charged: one for the seed and one for the successful successor.

docs.title: Interpret command exits correctly
docs.text:
CommandEvaluator owns one objective and an evaluator-owned grader outside the candidate tree. The agent cannot read the grader or its test definitions. Exit 0 passes, exit 1 is a rankable failing score, and any other exit is an unrankable EvaluatorFailure. The task bounds trials and wall time; AncestorsOnly pushes bounded command output to later proposals as public development feedback. Those disclosed failures are not held-out evidence.

Grader result Recorded outcome Search may rank it? Exit 0 score=1.0 Yes Exit 1 score=0.0 plus bounded process evidence Yes Any other exit or grader fault EvaluatorFailure No

docs.title: Understand the capture boundary
docs.text:
The fixture edits a file, adds another, deletes an obsolete file, and leaves bytecode debris. The adapter removes .pyc and __pycache__ debris, then captures the whole workspace once. Only UTF-8 regular files are representable; binary files and symlinks produce InvalidOutput.

The capture occurs after the callback returns. Individual file writes are not artifacts and do not consume trials; together they become one immutable successor with one lineage edge back to the parent snapshot.

docs.title: Use a smaller proposer for a small edit
docs.text:
For a small deterministic edit, a mapping-style callable is enough:

def repair(tree: meta.SourceTree, _context):
    return meta.SourceTree({**tree, "intervals.py": fixed_source})

This callable replaces the entire snapshot value directly. It is convenient when the edit is already known, but it does not provide a cwd for tools that expect normal filesystem operations.

docs.title: Swap in a live SDK
docs.text:
A live SDK changes only the factory implementation:

def build_agent(instructions):
    def edit(cwd, context):
        your_sdk.run(prompt=instructions, cwd=cwd, timeout_seconds=30)
    return WorkspaceProposer(edit)
Illustrative shape — live run, nothing captured
<provider session edits captured as one successor>

The evaluator, external tests, task, and budget stay fixed. A timeout or policy refusal from the SDK should become its matching typed failure, never a fake failing score.

As a prediction exercise, make the callback leave a non-UTF-8 file in the workspace. Capture will reject the proposal as InvalidOutput; the external grader will not receive a rankable successor.

Next, learn to inspect and compare.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
You will upgrade mechanical checks to a transparent rubric while keeping hard content gates, infrastructure failures, and held-out evaluation distinct.

The evaluator first rejects ungrounded content from the ranking by assigning a rankable overall = 0. It then records empathy, action, timeline, and concise criteria. A non-text response is different: it is InvalidOutput with no score. An exception in the grader becomes an evaluator failure.

The example keeps all judgment inside an ordinary evaluator callable. There is no separate rubric API: the task declares metric names, and the evaluator returns an EvaluationResult containing measurements and evidence.

docs.title: Complete rubric experiment
docs.text:
"""A richer, still deterministic evaluator for the support-response job."""

from __future__ import annotations

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import InvalidOutput


SEED = (
    "I'm sorry about the duplicate $49 charge for order #4021. "
    "I'm looking into it."
)
RESPONSES = (
    "I'm sorry about the duplicate $49 charge for order #4021. "
    "I'll submit a $49 refund today; it should appear in 5–7 business days.",
    "I understand the duplicate $49 charge on order #4021 is frustrating. "
    "I'll request a $49 refund within one business day.",
)


def _false_completion(reply: str) -> bool:
    lowered = reply.lower()
    return any(
        phrase in lowered
        for phrase in ("already refunded", "refund is complete", "refund was issued")
    )


def grade_response(reply: object) -> meta.EvaluationResult:
    """Apply content gates, then record four inspectable rubric criteria."""

    if not isinstance(reply, str):
        return meta.EvaluationResult(
            failure=InvalidOutput(message="support response must be text")
        )

    lowered = reply.lower()
    grounded = "#4021" in reply and "$49" in reply and not _false_completion(reply)
    criteria = {
        "empathy": float("sorry" in lowered or "understand" in lowered),
        "action": float("refund" in lowered and any(
            word in lowered for word in ("submit", "request", "will refund")
        )),
        "timeline": float(any(word in lowered for word in ("today", "day", "week"))),
        "concise": float(len(reply.split()) <= 35),
    }
    overall = sum(criteria.values()) / len(criteria) if grounded else 0.0
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"overall": overall, "grounded": float(grounded), **criteria},
        evidence=(
            meta.EvidenceDraft(
                kind="rubric/v1",
                data={"content_gate": grounded, "criteria": criteria},
            ),
        ),
    )


def propose_response(_parent: str, context: meta.ProposerContext) -> str:
    """Choose reproducibly; a different random seed exercises strategy B."""

    return context.rng.choice(RESPONSES)


def support_task() -> meta.Task:
    return meta.Task(
        evaluator=grade_response,
        objectives=(
            meta.Maximize("overall"),
            meta.Maximize("grounded"),
            meta.Maximize("empathy"),
            meta.Maximize("action"),
            meta.Maximize("timeline"),
            meta.Maximize("concise"),
        ),
        budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=3, trials=2),
    )


def run_support(*, random_seed: int = 0) -> meta.Run:
    return meta.run(
        meta.Experiment(
            task=support_task(),
            seed=SEED,
            proposer=propose_response,
            search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=2),
            random_seed=random_seed,
        )
    )


def held_out(candidate: str) -> float:
    """A separate final check that never steers the development run."""

    return float("5–7 business days" in candidate and "today" in candidate)


def run_held_out(candidate: str) -> meta.Run:
    return meta.improve(
        seed=candidate,
        proposer=lambda parent: parent,
        evaluator=held_out,
        trials=0,
    )


def main() -> None:
    result = run_support()
    trial = result.best_trial()
    print(f"seed_overall={result.trials()[0].metrics['overall']:.2f}")
    print(f"overall={trial.metrics['overall']:.2f}")
    print(f"criteria={dict(trial.metrics)}")
    print(f"evidence={trial.evidence[0].kind}")
    print(f"held_out={run_held_out(result.best().value).best_trial().metrics['score']:.0f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text:
The seed's overall=0.50 is intentional. It is grounded in the correct order and amount and is concise and empathetic, but it lacks a refund action and a timeline. The winning successor receives 1.00 on every declared criterion. The rubric/v1 evidence preserves the content-gate decision and criterion measurements that produced the score.

held_out=1 comes from a new run after selection. It does not retroactively steer the development search. In a real application, that second evaluator can own data that neither the proposer nor development evaluator may inspect.

docs.title: Combine signals without changing their meaning
docs.text:
This is one development experiment plus a separate held-out run. It shows the three honest ways to mix signals:

  • Put non-negotiable content gates inside the evaluator and make their failure a valid, rankable zero.
  • Declare extra metrics so they remain inspectable without steering search.
  • Measure held-out behavior in another run, after candidate selection.

Only Task.objectives[0] controls default ranking and satisfy= stopping. Later objectives are not a lexicographic tie-breaker; query them explicitly. The seed scores a fractional 0.5, proving the rubric is a gradient rather than only pass/fail.

Evaluator outcome Ranked? Meaning overall=0 after a wrong order, amount, or completion claim Yes Valid text failed a hard content gate Fractional overall with criterion metrics Yes Valid text has partial rubric quality InvalidOutput No The value is not a response the evaluator can judge EvaluatorFailure No The grading process did not produce a trustworthy result

This distinction protects search from treating “the grader crashed” as “the candidate was bad.” It also keeps hard gates useful: a grounded but weak reply can expose a gradient, while an unsafe reply remains rankable at zero.

docs.title: Replace only the judging implementation
docs.text:
An illustrative live judge can occupy the same callable seam; its exact output is provider-dependent and is not a runnable example command:

def live_judge(reply):
    raw = your_sdk.grade(reply, criteria=("empathy", "action", "timeline", "concise"))
    return parse_and_validate_evaluation_result(raw)
Illustrative shape — live run, nothing captured
<validated metrics and rubric/v1 evidence from your provider>

The wrapper must validate the provider response before constructing EvaluationResult. Malformed judge output is InvalidOutput; an SDK or service exception is EvaluatorFailure. Neither should be converted into a zero.

docs.title: Change one response and predict
docs.text:
Pass "I'll submit a $49 refund for order #9999 today." to grade_response(). It is well-formed text, so it remains rankable, but the content gate sets grounded=0 and overall=0. No typed failure is created.

Next, repair code with an agent.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
You will compare two controlled support-response runs and see an evaluator change refused before it can produce a misleading conclusion.

compare() does not decide whether two arbitrary scores are scientifically comparable. It first checks the recorded declarations that must match, then returns a comparison over the two successful summaries. This example changes only the recorded random seed, producing deterministic strategy A and B runs.

docs.title: Complete comparison program
docs.text:
The scorer, initial response, proposer declaration, objectives, and budget stay fixed:

"""Compare two compatible support runs and reject a changed evaluator."""

from __future__ import annotations

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.errors import RunsNotComparable

from rubric import SEED, grade_response, propose_response, run_support, support_task


def changed_evaluator_run() -> meta.Run:
    def changed_grader(candidate):
        return grade_response(candidate)

    task = support_task()
    return meta.run(
        meta.Experiment(
            task=meta.Task(
                evaluator=changed_grader,
                objectives=task.objectives,
                budget=task.budget,
            ),
            seed=SEED,
            proposer=propose_response,
            search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=2),
        )
    )


def main() -> None:
    strategy_a = run_support(random_seed=0)
    strategy_b = run_support(random_seed=1)
    comparison = strategy_a.compare(strategy_b)
    print(f"compatible_result={'tie' if comparison.tied else 'winner'}")
    print(f"same_random_seed={comparison.same_random_seed}")
    try:
        strategy_a.compare(changed_evaluator_run())
    except RunsNotComparable:
        print("changed_evaluator=refused")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Read the comparison
docs.text:
compatible_result=tie means both runs achieved the same primary overall score. It does not mean their histories are byte-identical. The next line makes the intended difference explicit: the random seeds differ, and the comparison record reports that fact.

The final line is a different situation. changed_evaluator_run() wraps the same apparent grading behavior in a different evaluator declaration. Meta-Evolve refuses the comparison because changing the measuring instrument invalidates the controlled score comparison; it does not guess that two callables are “close enough.”

docs.title: Know what must stay fixed
docs.text:
A comparison is one experiment: change one intended variable and keep the task, evaluator, proposer declaration, initial artifact, primary objective, and effective budget compatible. Meta-Evolve refuses incompatible comparisons; it cannot detect hidden differences inside two name-only closures.

Must match May differ and is reported Evaluator and primary objective Search declaration Task and effective budget Random seed Artifact kind and initial content Context policy Proposer identity Experience declaration

Runs with typed failures can still be inspected individually. A comparison needs a successful evaluation on both sides; NoSuccessfulEvaluation means there is no score to compare, while RunsNotComparable means the declarations do not describe a controlled comparison.

For winner, lineage, usage, and unrankable-run diagnosis, use What a run returns; a selected result is still only a recorded candidate, not a deployment.

docs.title: Change one declaration and predict
docs.text:
Run both arms with random_seed=0. Comparison remains allowed, and same_random_seed becomes True. Change the evaluator instead and comparison is refused before a winner or tie is reported.

Next, swap one part deliberately.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
You will run controlled component changes and see where comparison accepts or refuses them.

The playground uses a deliberately small integer task so component behavior is visible without domain noise. Every run begins at 0 and uses the same scoring function and task budget. Each output line changes one declared seam or one execution overlay.

docs.title: Complete playground
docs.text:
"""Controlled swaps over one small experiment declaration."""

from __future__ import annotations

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.errors import RunsNotComparable
from meta_evolve.policies import AncestorsOnly, BestOfN


BUDGET = meta.Budget(evaluations=4, trials=3)


def score(value: int) -> meta.EvaluationResult:
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"score": float(value)},
        evidence=(
            meta.EvidenceDraft(
                kind="public-check/v1",
                data={"failure": "value is still below the target"},
            ),
        ),
    )


def changed_score(value: int) -> float:
    return float(value * 2)


def add_one(parent: int, _context) -> int:
    return parent + 1


def jump_two(parent: int, _context) -> int:
    return parent + 2


@meta.search(max_trials=3, parent="incumbent")
def refine_incumbent(search):
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)


def experiment(*, proposer=add_one, search=None, evaluator=score, context=None):
    return meta.Experiment(
        task=meta.Task(evaluator=evaluator, budget=BUDGET),
        seed=0,
        proposer=proposer,
        search=search or meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
        context=context,
        random_seed=7,
    )


def main() -> None:
    strategy_a = meta.run(experiment(proposer=add_one))
    strategy_b = meta.run(experiment(proposer=jump_two))
    greedy = strategy_a
    best_of_n = meta.run(experiment(search=BestOfN(max_trials=3)))
    custom = meta.run(experiment(search=refine_incumbent))
    with_feedback = meta.run(experiment(context=AncestorsOnly()))
    narrower = meta.run(experiment(), budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=2, trials=1))

    print(f"proposers={strategy_a.best().value},{strategy_b.best().value}")
    print(f"policies={greedy.best().value},{best_of_n.best().value},{custom.best().value}")
    print(f"context_same={greedy.compare(with_feedback).same_context_declaration}")
    print(f"narrow_usage={narrower.summary().evaluation_count}")

    try:
        greedy.compare(meta.run(experiment(evaluator=changed_score)))
    except RunsNotComparable:
        print("changed_evaluator=refused")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text:
Output What changed What it demonstrates proposers=3,6 Add one versus jump two Different proposer strategies can produce different outcomes, but their incompatible identities are not passed to compare() policies=3,1,3 Greedy, BestOfN, functional search Parent choice changes the reachable result under the same task context_same=False No context versus AncestorsOnly The comparison is allowed and records that the context declaration changed narrow_usage=2 Narrower call-level budget The seed plus one successor consume two evaluations changed_evaluator=refused Different scoring callable The measuring instrument changed, so comparison is invalid

BestOfN keeps proposing from the seed, so three add-one attempts all reach 1. Greedy feeds each accepted incumbent back to the proposer and reaches 3. The functional @search rule explicitly chooses the incumbent and therefore matches the Greedy result here.

The narrower run budget does not mutate the reusable experiment declaration. It can reduce the task's allowed work for one execution, but it cannot widen the task budget.

docs.title: Separate run failures from comparison refusal
docs.text: Component exceptions and malformed outputs remain typed run outcomes; a comparison refusal is instead a declaration error about experimental validity. The former says an attempt did not produce a rankable measurement. The latter says two otherwise valid runs should not be summarized as a controlled A/B.

docs.title: Change one part and predict
docs.text:
Change BestOfN(max_trials=3) to BestOfN(max_trials=1). Its best value stays 1, because every attempt starts from the seed, but its usage decreases. If you change both the policy and evaluator at once, you can still run both jobs, but compare() will refuse to attribute their score difference to search.

Next, choose the focused How-to for the one seam you need to customize. Configured-model identity is an advanced comparison trap covered in Common traps, not syntax needed for this job.

docs.title: Build an autoresearch loop with Meta-Evolve
docs.text:
Suppose you already have an agent that can improve a solution. How would you test changes to the research procedure itself without letting that procedure change its own benchmark, budget, or promotion rule?

This chapter builds the smallest complete answer. It runs offline in a fraction of a second.

The design is inspired by Weco's AIDE² report. It borrows the report's inner-task/outer-researcher experimental shape with fixed cost and private selection. It does not reproduce AIDE² or provide evidence of recursive self-improvement.

docs.title: The result first
docs.text:
Run this from the repository root:

RunResult 
uv run python examples/research/autoresearch/main.py

autoresearch teaching run: outer=(evaluations=3,trials=2) inner=(evaluations=5,trials=4)
recipe=(1,) public={'public-large': 0.14285714285714285, 'public-small': 0.3333333333333333} private_quality=0.180556
recipe=(1, 2) public={'public-large': 0.2, 'public-small': 1.0} private_quality=0.321429
recipe=(1, 2, 4) public={'public-large': 0.3333333333333333, 'public-small': 0.5} private_quality=0.600000
selected=(1, 2, 4)
held_out_baseline={'held-out-small': 0.16666666666666666, 'held-out-large': 0.09090909090909091}
held_out_selected={'held-out-small': 0.5, 'held-out-large': 0.14285714285714285}
promotion=none

The selected recipe does better in this constructed example. That shows the wiring works; it is not a scientific result.

Each trial retains only its autoresearch-public-report record as candidate-visible evidence.

docs.title: The two levels
docs.text:
“Inner” and “outer” describe which thing is being improved:

outer Meta-Evolve run
│
├─ artifact: a recipe for conducting inner research
├─ proposer: change that recipe once
├─ evaluator: measure the changed researcher under a fixed protocol
└─ search: retain a recipe only when private quality improves
       │
       ├─ inner run on public task A
       ├─ inner run on public task B
       ├─ inner run on private task A
       └─ inner run on private task B

after outer selection
├─ seed researcher on held-out tasks
├─ selected researcher on the same held-out tasks
└─ report the comparison; promote nothing

An inner run improves an integer on a small black-box landscape. The candidate research recipe says which move sizes it may try. (1,) makes slow local progress. (1, 2, 4) can cover more distance under the same four-trial limit.

The integer task is intentionally unimportant. In a real project, replace it with model training, a solver, a coding agent, or another measured research task. The outer contract stays the same.

docs.title: The five Meta-Evolve declarations
docs.text:
The outer loop uses the ordinary public API:

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(
        evaluator=evaluate_researcher,
        artifact=meta.Text,
        objectives=(meta.Maximize("private_quality"),),
        budget=OUTER_BUDGET,
    ),
    seed=SEED,
    proposer=propose_researcher,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=OUTER_TRIALS),
    context=meta.policies.AncestorsOnly(max_records=CONTEXT_RECORDS),
    random_seed=0,
)
return meta.run(experiment)

Read it as a sentence: Task fixes evaluation and limits; SEED is the starting recipe; propose_researcher proposes a successor; Greedy retains improvements; and AncestorsOnly supplies public reports from parent lineage.

The coordinator records every candidate, score, proposal hypothesis, evidence reference, decision, usage total, and causal parent.

docs.title: The candidate-controlled surface
docs.text:
The complete mutable artifact is tiny JSON:

{"moves":[1,2,4]}

decode permits only the moves key, one to four integer moves, and values between 1 and 8. An invalid recipe produces a typed InvalidOutput with no metric, so malformed output can never outrank a valid researcher.

Everything else is experiment-controlled:

Control Owner Move recipe Candidate Public, private, and held-out tasks Evaluator Inner and outer budgets Experiment private_quality calculation Evaluator Greedy admission Search policy Whether a winner is deployed Governance / user

This separation is the safety and validity mechanism. “Self-improvement” does not mean self-authorized evaluation or deployment.

docs.title: One candidate evaluation
docs.text:
evaluate_researcher first validates the recipe. It then performs four inner runs under byte-identical declarations:

public = score(researcher, PUBLIC_TASKS)
private = score(researcher, PRIVATE_TASKS)
return EvaluationResult(
    metrics={"private_quality": fmean(private.values())},
    evidence=(
        EvidenceDraft(
            kind=PUBLIC_REPORT,
            data={"scores": public, "inner_trials_per_task": INNER_TRIALS},
        ),
    ),
)

Public per-task outcomes become inspectable evidence. Private task names, targets, and per-task outcomes are not placed in evidence. The outer search policy receives only their aggregate metric for selection.

The deterministic proposer extracts only autoresearch-public-report records. Its ProposalResult.derived_from points to the report it used. This preserves the causal claim “this change was based on that observation.”

docs.title: Exact budget arithmetic
docs.text:
The seed and two successors give the outer run:

3 outer evaluations = 1 seed + 2 proposals
2 outer trials      = 2 proposals

Each outer evaluation runs four benchmark tasks. Each task permits the seed plus four inner proposals:

5 inner evaluations per task
× 4 tasks per outer evaluation
× 3 outer evaluations
= 60 inner evaluations used for selection at most

After selection, the seed and winner each run on two held-out tasks:

5 × 2 policies × 2 held-out tasks = 20 post-selection evaluations at most

The nested runs own their own hard budgets. The outer budget counts outer candidate evaluations; it does not pretend that a nested benchmark call is one unit of physical work. A production setup should additionally aggregate token, GPU-hour, dollar, and wall-clock usage at the evaluator boundary.

docs.title: Why three task splits?
docs.text:
The public tasks provide feedback for proposing the next researcher. The private tasks decide whether the proposal survives. Held-out tasks are touched only after the search has selected a winner.

Split Candidate model may see details? Affects selection? Public Yes Indirectly, through proposals Private No Yes, through aggregate quality Held-out No during search No

If the outer model sees private targets or per-task results, “private” is only a label. If held-out results influence another proposal, those tasks have become part of development and a new untouched suite is required.

docs.title: Replacing the deterministic proposer with an agent
docs.text:
The deterministic proposer keeps CI credential-free. A model-backed wrapper should preserve this boundary:

ProposerContext → allowlisted public evidence → private workspace
  → one bounded agent session → validated ProposalResult
  → derived_from references and usage

Do not give the model raw outer context because it contains the aggregate private metric needed by trusted search. Build an allowlisted workspace. The prompt-optimization example shows how a callable outer proposer can run a bounded source-tree agent one level down and lift the result back into meta.Text.

For a source-code researcher, change the artifact to meta.SourceTree, use an exact mutation allowlist, and evaluate each candidate in a fresh workspace. Keep benchmark source, credentials, permissions, and promotion controls outside that tree.

docs.title: What the comparison may claim
docs.text:
This tiny example supports one narrow statement: under the declared toy tasks and equal inner budgets, the selected recipe has higher private and held-out quality than the seed.

It does not establish real-domain autonomy, superiority to experts, statistical robustness, out-of-distribution generalization, accelerating improvement, reward-hacking safety, or readiness for automatic deployment.

Those claims require larger protocols, repeated runs, fixed physical costs, external baselines, untouched tasks, and adversarial checks. Negative results, ties, typed failures, and rejected proposals must remain in the record.

docs.title: Relationship to harness evolution
docs.text:
This is a deliberately smaller composition built from meta.Text, nested meta.run, typed evidence and failures, lineage, budgets, and an ordinary search policy. It introduces no harness type or runtime behavior.

The harness API supplies plain frozen Harness values, example-owned episode suites, strict held-out comparison, and safe export. This chapter stays as the explicitly small recipe-evolution composition; the canonical harness story is the M8 guide.

docs.title: Leakage and validity checklist
docs.text:
Before adapting the pattern, answer these questions:

  1. Can candidate code read private task files, environment variables, grader output, or prior held-out results?
  2. Are baseline and candidate evaluated on exactly the same tasks, seeds, model identity, tool permissions, and physical budget?
  3. Can a candidate increase concurrency, retries, context, or model calls and thereby buy a better score?
  4. Are malformed output, timeout, policy violation, and infrastructure failure unrankable typed outcomes rather than zeros?
  5. Does every proposal identify the public evidence it actually used?
  6. Is held-out evaluation run once after selection and excluded from promotion unless promotion policy explicitly owns it?

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text: Change INNER_TRIALS from 4 to 2, update INNER_BUDGET consistently, and predict which recipe wins before rerunning the example. Then ask whether the winner changed because its research strategy is generally better or because the experiment changed the resource regime.

docs.title: First run: a function that is still wrong
docs.text:
The support quickstart showed the loop. This advanced lab keeps one program: repair below_zero, a HumanEval-shaped bank-balance check. The seed returns sum(operations) < 0. That misses a dip that later recovers, so the score is a fraction, not a pass/fail cliff.

result = meta.improve(
    seed=seed_text(),
    proposer=climb,
    evaluator=evaluate,
    trials=1,
)

The proposer applies one tempting patch: treat any negative number as a failure. One successor attempt is not enough to finish the job.

RunResult 
uv run python examples/learn/below_zero/stages/01_improve.py

7/9
['4/9', '7/9']

The seed is 4/9. The tempting patch is 7/9. The run worked, and the best result is still wrong. trials=1 is a bound, not a declaration of success.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Raise trials to 2 and keep this proposer. Predict a perfect score: the second patch is a running balance, and greedy will apply it from 7/9.

Back to Examples · Next: Name better

docs.title: Name what better means
docs.text:
improve() maximizes the evaluator's scalar as score. Expand to a Task when the metric name or a satisfaction threshold matters. That call is exactly this declaration:

task = meta.Task(
    evaluator=evaluate,
    artifact=meta.Text,
    objectives=(meta.Maximize("pass_rate", satisfy=1.0),),
)
experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed=seed_text(),
    proposer=climb,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=8),
)
result = meta.run(experiment)

Use the expansion from here on. Task owns evaluator semantics; it is not a second evaluator. satisfy=1.0 stops the run when every test passes.

RunResult 
uv run python examples/learn/below_zero/stages/02_task.py

9/9
complete
2

Two successor attempts reach a perfect score, so the run stops. The remaining six permitted trials are unspent.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Remove satisfy=1.0. The same 9/9 can still rank best, but reaching it no longer declares the objective satisfied; the run continues until search stops.

Previous: First run · Next: Change search

docs.title: Change only search
docs.text:
Keep Task, seed, and proposer fixed. Change only the search= field:

greedy = meta.Experiment(
    task=task, seed=seed_text(), proposer=climb, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3)
)
independent = meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed=seed_text(),
    proposer=climb,
    search=meta.policies.BestOfN(max_trials=3),
)

Greedy expands the current best, so the tempting 7/9 patch can be repaired. BestOfN always expands the seed — HumanEval's pass@k in this vocabulary — and keeps resampling that same first patch.

RunResult 
uv run python examples/learn/below_zero/stages/03_search.py

Greedy best: 9/9
BestOfN best: 7/9
Greedy lineage: (4, 7, 9)
BestOfN lineage: (4, 7)
same proposer: climb
same evaluator: evaluate

Generation and evaluation did not change. Lineage did. Use Population when several ranked branches matter. Use @meta.search only when none of these presets is the decision.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Give BestOfN twenty trials. Predict the winner stays 7/9: every proposal still starts from the seed, so the running-balance repair is never reached.

Previous: Name better · Next: Hide some tests

docs.title: Hide some tests from the proposer
docs.text:
The same function now travels as a SourceTree. Public cases may appear as evidence. Hidden cases change pass_rate and never appear in that evidence — the EvalPlus reason for extra tests, on this one problem.

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(
        evaluator=evaluate,
        artifact=meta.SourceTree,
        objectives=(meta.Maximize("pass_rate", satisfy=1.0),),
    ),
    seed=seed_tree(),
    proposer=climb,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
)

The grader stays a callable. Hidden tests live in evaluate.py, outside the tree. A subprocess CommandEvaluator is the source-repair track, not this page.

RunResult 
uv run python examples/learn/below_zero/stages/04_hidden.py

seed score: 4/9
public failures: 3
hidden in evidence: False
hardcoded: 7/9 public 0

A solution that special-cases the public list can look clean in evidence and still lose on hidden cases. The candidate does not own the metric.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Add the three hidden inputs to the public suite. Predict the hardcoded patch's evidence is no longer empty: those cases become feedback, not measurement.

Previous: Change search · Next: Use failures

docs.title: Use failures through the kernel
docs.text:
Without experience, this proposer always applies the tempting any-negative patch. Experience is off by default. It improves the seed to 7/9 and then repeats that patch. That repeated mistake is the reason to add memory.

blind = meta.Experiment(
    task=task, seed=seed_tree(), proposer=from_failures, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3)
)
informed = meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed=seed_tree(),
    proposer=from_failures,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
    context=meta.policies.AncestorsOnly(max_records=20, max_chars=8000),
)

AncestorsOnly pushes bounded ancestor records before each proposal. The proposer reads public failure messages from that bundle. It never imports evaluate.py.

RunResult 
uv run python examples/learn/below_zero/stages/05_failures.py

no context: 7/9
pushed failures: 9/9
same proposer: from_failures

The never-below case [1, -1] only appears after the tempting patch. Pushed evidence lets the next proposal skip it. Pull access and declared derivation belong on the Program the loop track.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Set max_records=1. Predict the informed run stays at 7/9: the never-below failure is not in the truncated bundle, so the proposer repeats the same patch.

Previous: Hide some tests · Next: Inspect and compare

docs.title: Inspect results and compare runs
docs.text:
A Run answers both “what ranked best?” and “what happened?”

greedy = meta.run(meta.Experiment(
    task=task, seed=seed_tree(), proposer=climb, search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3)
))
independent = meta.run(meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed=seed_tree(),
    proposer=climb,
    search=meta.policies.BestOfN(max_trials=3),
))
print(greedy.lineage())
print(greedy.compare(independent).winner is not None)

best() is the selected artifact; best().value is its payload. best_trial() includes the winning evaluation. trials() includes the seed, losers, and typed failures. lineage() is the causal path to the winner. summary() and summary().usage report compact totals. inspect() works when a run is failed or unrankable. compare() ranks compatible declarations and keeps search as the visible difference.

RunResult 
uv run python examples/learn/below_zero/main.py

Greedy best: 9/9
BestOfN best: 7/9
lineage(): (4, 7, 9)
inspect(): rankable
compare(): Greedy
failure: ('trial_failed', 'InvalidOutput')
failed inspect(): rankable

An invalid proposal records InvalidOutput with no artifact. It is not a low score. The successfully evaluated seed keeps the run rankable.

docs.text:
Make the evaluator raise. Predict EvaluatorFailure on every trial, then inspect() reports unrankable and best() raises NoSuccessfulEvaluation.
